name: KYC and financial crime operations
bg: periodic reviews are overdue for 400 corporate clients and the regulator flagged it; if it slips, we face a formal finding
aud: Client onboarding and periodic review teams in Operations (first line of defence), usually in onboarding hubs; relationship managers in Corporate, Commercial and Private Banking whose clients wait on KYC
fun: Client Onboarding / KYC Operations as process owner, Financial Crime Compliance as second-line oversight, and the client-facing businesses
ben: faster client onboarding; clearing the backlog of overdue periodic reviews; consistent quality of KYC files; flexible capacity for peaks and remediation
kpi: turnaround time per case (onboarding and periodic review); backlog and overdue reviews; quality-check pass rate; rework rate
sl: Standard cases completed within 5 working days and high-risk cases within 10; at least 98% of files pass quality checks; overdue periodic reviews reduced to zero by an agreed date
reg: Evidence for regulators that customer due diligence is complete and on time; a clear audit trail per client file; fewer findings on overdue reviews
out: Final risk-rating and client acceptance decisions, which stay with the bank; exit decisions for clients; changes to our onboarding systems
qual: Analysts trained in customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence; recognised AML certification (for example ACAMS) for team leads; background-checked staff
personal: client names, ID documents, addresses, ownership structures and source-of-wealth information
important: KYC and financial crime work, which large banks usually treat as supporting a critical or important function
deps: Access to the onboarding and screening systems; our KYC procedures and risk-rating rules; a named Financial Crime Compliance contact for escalations
notes: Usually run in Operations hubs, often nearshore or offshore; client data access makes data protection and outsourcing reviews likely; regulators expect the bank to keep the risk decisions.
mh: case management with an audit trail per client file, four-eyes review on high-risk cases, and daily backlog reporting

name: Payments and securities operations
bg: payment exceptions pile up at month end and cut-offs are missed; if it slips, clients are paid late
aud: Payments, settlements and reconciliations teams in Operations, and the businesses whose clients rely on timely payments
fun: Operations (process owner), Treasury and Finance, with Operational Risk oversight
ben: fewer failed or late payments; faster investigation of exceptions; capacity for volume peaks
kpi: straight-through processing rate; exceptions cleared within the cut-off; open reconciliation breaks by age; failed settlements
sl: All items processed before the daily cut-off; 99.9% accuracy; reconciliation breaks investigated within 1 working day
reg: Operational resilience for an important business service; a clear audit trail of every payment
out: Payment authorisation and release, which stay with the bank; changes to the payment systems
qual: Staff experienced in payments or securities operations at a bank; background-checked
personal: client account details, payment data and counterparties
important: payments and settlement work, which large banks usually treat as an important business service
deps: System access with dual control; cut-off times and procedures; a named Operations contact
notes: Money movement makes this high risk: dual control, access reviews and operational resilience requirements apply.
mh: processing within the payment cut-offs, exception handling with a full audit trail, and daily reconciliation reports

name: Accounts payable and finance operations
bg: invoices are paid late and we pay about €20,000 a year in late fees; if it slips, supplier complaints grow
aud: Accounts Payable and Finance Operations teams, and the suppliers and budget holders who wait on payment
fun: Finance (process owner), Procurement for the purchase-to-pay process, and Tax
ben: suppliers paid on time; fewer duplicate or wrong payments; less manual work at month end
kpi: invoices processed within the agreed days; first-time match rate; duplicate payments prevented; supplier queries closed on time
sl: 95% of invoices processed within 3 working days; accuracy of at least 99%; supplier queries answered within 2 working days
reg: Clean controls for the annual audit; correct VAT treatment
out: Approval and payment release, which stay with us; changes to our finance systems
qual: Staff experienced in accounts payable for large companies; background-checked
personal: supplier bank details and contact data
deps: Access to the finance system and invoice inbox; approval workflows; a named Finance contact
notes: Usually run from a finance shared-service centre; bank details make fraud controls important.
mh: three-way matching, duplicate-payment checks before release, and a full audit trail per invoice

name: HR operations and payroll
bg: payroll runs on an old tool and spreadsheets; if it slips, we miss the statutory reporting deadline
aud: HR operations and payroll teams, and all employees in the countries covered
fun: HR (process owner), Finance for payroll accounting, and Information Security
ben: accurate and on-time pay; less manual work; better employee experience
kpi: payroll accuracy; payroll delivered on time; employee queries closed on time
sl: Payroll 100% on time; accuracy of at least 99.9%; employee queries answered within 2 working days
reg: Compliance with tax and social security rules in each country; data protection for employee data
out: Pay and grading decisions, which stay with HR
qual: Payroll specialists for each country covered; background-checked
personal: employee names, salaries, bank details and personal records
important: payroll, which banks often treat as a critical service for staff
deps: Employee master data; pay rules per country; a named HR contact
notes: Employee data makes data protection reviews certain; multi-country payroll needs local expertise.
mh: payroll accuracy checks before each run, secure handling of employee data, and support for all our countries

name: Client contact centre
aud: Retail or wealth clients who call or write in, and the client service teams in Operations
fun: Client service / Operations, with Compliance for conduct and complaints handling
ben: shorter waiting times; consistent answers; capacity for peaks
kpi: calls answered within the target time; first-contact resolution; complaint handling time; client satisfaction
sl: 80% of calls answered within 30 seconds; complaints acknowledged within 1 working day and resolved within the regulatory deadline
reg: Fair treatment of clients and complaints handling to regulatory standards
out: Decisions on refunds or compensation beyond agreed limits
qual: Trained client service agents; product training for the bank's products; background-checked
personal: client names, account details and conversation records
important: client service, which large banks usually treat as an important business service
deps: Scripts and product information; access to client systems; escalation routes
notes: Conduct risk and client data access; call recording and complaint rules apply.
bg: complaints are rising and calls wait over five minutes at peak; if it slips, the regulator sees the complaint figures
mh: call recording and quality monitoring, complaint logging in our CRM, and service hours that match our clients' time zones

name: Regulatory reporting
aud: Regulatory Reporting and Finance teams, and the senior managers who sign off the returns
fun: Finance / Regulatory Reporting, with Risk for data and Compliance
ben: returns submitted on time and correct; less manual adjustment; fewer resubmissions
kpi: returns submitted on time; resubmissions; data quality issues closed
sl: All returns ready for sign-off 2 working days before the deadline
reg: Accurate and timely returns to supervisors; a clear data lineage
out: Sign-off and submission of returns, which stay with the bank
qual: Specialists in the relevant regulatory returns; experience at large banks
important: regulatory reporting, which supervisors expect to be resilient
deps: Source data and reconciliations; reporting calendar; a named Finance contact
notes: Senior managers stay accountable for the returns; deadlines are fixed by supervisors.
bg: a new reporting template applies from June and our team has no capacity; if it slips, we miss a regulatory deadline
mh: templates that follow the latest regulatory taxonomy, validation before submission, and an audit trail from source data to report

name: IT service desk and managed IT
aud: All colleagues who need IT support, and the Technology teams that run the services
ben: faster fixes; support around the clock; predictable cost
kpi: incidents resolved within target; first-contact resolution; user satisfaction; backlog of tickets
sl: Priority 1 incidents answered within 15 minutes and fixed within 4 hours; 80% of calls answered within 60 seconds
reg: Operational resilience and ICT risk management in line with regulatory expectations
out: Changes to systems outside the agreed services; hardware purchases
qual: ITIL-trained staff; certified engineers for the technologies supported; background-checked
personal: colleague names and contact details; possibly access to systems with client data
important: IT services that support banking systems, which may count as critical or important
deps: Access to the ticketing tool and systems; knowledge articles; escalation to our Technology teams
notes: ICT third-party risk rules apply (for example DORA in the EU); privileged access needs strict control.
bg: tickets wait three days and the current contract ends in April; if it slips, staff have no IT support
mh: one ticketing system with our own categories, 24/7 cover for priority 1 incidents, and monthly service reports

name: Cyber security services
aud: The Chief Information Security Office and the Technology teams responsible for the systems tested or monitored
fun: Information Security (owner), Technology, and Operational Risk
ben: risks found before attackers find them; faster detection and response; evidence for regulators and auditors
kpi: findings reported within the agreed time; critical findings fixed on time; detection and response times
sl: Critical findings reported within 24 hours; security incidents escalated within 15 minutes
reg: Evidence of testing and monitoring expected by supervisors; ICT risk requirements
out: Fixing the findings, unless agreed separately
qual: Certified testers (for example CREST or OSCP); security-cleared staff
personal: possibly client and employee data in the systems tested
deps: Scope and rules of engagement; test accounts and access; named Technology contacts
notes: Testers get privileged access; rules of engagement and confidentiality are essential.
bg: the annual penetration test is due before the audit; if it slips, the audit finding stays open
mh: testers with recognised certifications, findings rated by severity with fixes, and a retest of critical findings

name: Front-office trading platform
bg: our trading platform is end of life and vendor support ends next year; if it slips, we trade on unsupported software
aud: Traders, sales and structurers, with Middle Office, Market Risk and Operations using the trade data
fun: Front office (business owner), Technology, Market Risk, Operations and Compliance
ben: a supported, scalable platform in place of an end-of-life system; trades captured once and processed straight through; real-time positions and risk; fewer manual breaks between front and back office
kpi: straight-through processing rate; platform availability in trading hours; trade capture latency; number of manual trade breaks
sl: Availability of 99.95% in trading hours; priority 1 incidents answered within 15 minutes and fixed within 1 hour; month-end and market open covered
reg: Transaction reporting and best-execution evidence; complete records for market abuse surveillance; operational resilience for an important business service
out: Migration of historic trade data beyond the agreed period, unless agreed separately; changes to downstream finance and settlement systems; market data licences
qual: Delivery teams with experience of trading platform implementations at banks; certified on the chosen platform
personal: client names, accounts, positions and trading records
important: trading platforms, which large banks usually treat as supporting a critical or important function
deps: Access to booking, market data and reference data systems; a named front-office product owner; test environments and historic trade samples
mh: real-time trade capture and position keeping, pre-trade limit checks and integration with booking and market data; it works if 98% of trades go straight through
notes: Trading platforms are usually run by the bank (licensed) or hosted by the vendor (SaaS); hosting decides whether outsourcing and DORA rules apply in full.

name: Trading voice and call recording
aud: Traders, sales and other front-office staff whose calls and messages must be recorded, and the Compliance surveillance team
fun: Front office, Technology for voice and mobile, and Compliance for record keeping and surveillance
ben: complete records of client and trading conversations; faster retrieval for investigations and complaints; one service across desks
kpi: share of required calls and messages recorded; time to retrieve a requested record; recording outages
sl: Recording available 99.9% of trading hours; a requested record retrieved within 1 working day; outages reported within 1 hour
reg: Record keeping of telephone conversations and electronic communications for investment services, kept for at least five years (up to seven if the supervisor asks); evidence for conduct investigations
out: Surveillance analysis of the recordings, unless agreed separately; handsets, unless agreed separately
qual: Experience recording regulated trading communications at banks; background-checked staff
personal: recorded conversations with clients and colleagues, phone numbers and message content
deps: A list of the users and devices in scope; our retention rules; a named Compliance contact
notes: Recordings must be complete, kept unaltered and retrievable for the whole retention period; gaps in recording must be reported.
bg: our call-recording platform is end of life and misses mobile calls; if it slips, we breach the record-keeping rules
mh: complete recording of fixed and mobile lines, search and replay within minutes, and retention for the regulatory period

name: Security guarding
aud: Everyone working at or visiting the sites covered, and the site security team
fun: Corporate Security and Corporate Real Estate
ben: safe and secure sites; controlled access for staff and visitors; fast response to incidents
kpi: posts staffed as scheduled; incident response times; access-control breaches
sl: All posts staffed for 100% of scheduled hours; alarms answered within 5 minutes; incident reports within 24 hours
reg: Duty of care for staff and visitors; physical security of the bank's premises
out: Building maintenance and cleaning; IT security monitoring
qual: Guards licensed under local law and background-checked; trained in first aid and fire safety
personal: visitor and staff names, access records and CCTV images
deps: Site plans and security procedures; access to the access-control system; a named site security contact
notes: When the provider changes, guards may transfer to the new provider by law; allow for this in the timeline and costs.
bg: the guarding contract for two sites ends in March; if it slips, the sites are unstaffed
mh: licensed and background-checked guards, posts staffed for every scheduled hour, and incident reports within 24 hours
